glossary.def: A programmatic check between steps of a chain that validates an intermediate result before the next call runs.
A parallelisation variant that splits a task into independent subtasks and runs them at the same time.
A parallelisation variant that runs the same task several times and combines the outputs, for higher confidence.
A loop that interleaves reasoning with tool actions: think, act, observe, repeat until the answer is supported.
A loop shape where a planner writes the steps first, an executor runs them and a replan step handles surprises.
An approach that stores verbal self-reflections in an episodic memory buffer and reuses them on the next attempt, with no weight updates.
A loop where one agent produces work and another checks it against criteria. Also called evaluator-optimizer, generator-verifier or critic loop.
The typed cause for ending a run, such as completed, max steps, budget, deadline, repeat or needs human. Returned with the best partial result.
A central agent that owns the conversation and calls specialist agents as tools. Control returns to it after each call.
The orchestrator in a group chat that picks the next speaker and decides when to stop.
In Magentic orchestration, the manager's per-round record of whether the task is done, stalled or needs another agent.
The Multi-Agent System Failure Taxonomy: 14 failure modes in three categories, built from annotated multi-agent traces.
Choosing what enters the model's window at each step: instructions, tools, memory, retrieved data, history and tool results.
The idea that context is finite with diminishing returns, so every token competes for the model's attention.
Removing stale tool outputs from context, ideally keeping a pointer so they can be fetched again.
What the model holds in its context window for the current step, including the scratchpad and plan.
Long-term facts and preferences that stay true across sessions, such as a user's preferred units.
Planting malicious or misleading entries in an agent's long-term memory or knowledge store so they steer later runs.
A saved snapshot of run state that lets a run resume after a crash, restart or long wait.
A runtime model that persists progress, retries failed steps, supports long timers and replays deterministic orchestration code.
A point where a human must approve a proposed action, ideally bound to the exact arguments, before it runs.
A step that undoes the effect of an earlier completed step when a later step of the operation fails.

claims.text: Anthropic defines workflows as LLMs and tools orchestrated through predefined code paths, and agents as systems where the LLM dynamically directs its own process and tool use.

The Azure Architecture Center lists three levels (direct model call, single agent with tools, multiagent orchestration), says to use the lowest level that reliably meets requirements, and calls a single agent with tools often the right default for enterprise use cases.

OpenAI says to maximise a single agent's capabilities first and to split when prompts hold many if-then-else branches or tool selection fails after clearer descriptions. Some systems manage more than 15 distinct tools while others struggle with fewer than 10 overlapping ones.

Anthropic's multi-agent research system (Opus 4 lead, Sonnet 4 subagents) beat single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2 percent on its internal research eval, and used about 15x the tokens of chat (agents about 4x). Vendor-reported.
Token usage alone explained 80 percent of the variance in BrowseComp performance in Anthropic's analysis.

Anthropic's prompt rules scale effort to difficulty: 1 agent with 3 to 10 tool calls for simple fact-finding, 2 to 4 subagents with 10 to 15 calls for comparisons, and more than 10 subagents for complex research.

Cognition's 2026-04-22 post says parallel-writer swarms still fail, multiple agents contributing intelligence works when writes stay single-threaded, and its review loop catches on average 2 bugs per PR (about 58 percent severe), best when the reviewer shares no context with the coder. Vendor-reported.
RouteLLM reports that trained routers between a stronger and a weaker model reduce cost by over 2x in certain cases without compromising response quality.
Self-consistency reports +17.9 percent on GSM8K over greedy chain-of-thought prompting.

The Azure guide names maker-checker loops as also known as evaluator-optimizer, generator-verifier, critic loops and reflection loops, and requires clear acceptance criteria, an iteration cap and defined fallback behaviour.
The Azure guide recommends limiting group chat orchestration to three or fewer agents and avoiding it when the chat manager has no objective way to tell that the task is complete.
ReAct reports absolute success-rate gains of 34 percent on ALFWorld and 10 percent on WebShop over imitation and reinforcement-learning baselines, with one or two in-context examples.
ReWOO reports 5x token efficiency and 4 percent higher accuracy on HotpotQA versus interleaved reasoning.
Reflexion reports 91 percent pass@1 on HumanEval versus 80 percent for the GPT-4 baseline, using verbal reflections in an episodic memory buffer with no weight updates.
Self-Refine reports about 20 percent absolute average improvement across seven tasks using one model as generator, feedback provider and refiner.
Huang et al. find that LLMs struggle to self-correct reasoning without external feedback, and performance sometimes degrades after self-correction.
The OpenAI Agents SDK raises MaxTurnsExceeded when max_turns is exceeded, and max_turns=None disables the limit.
LangGraph's recursion limit caps super-steps per execution, raises GraphRecursionError, and defaults to 1000 steps from version 1.0.6.
OpenAI advises reserving at least 25,000 tokens for reasoning plus output when starting out, and hitting max_output_tokens returns status incomplete, possibly before any visible output.

Agent Framework group chat uses a star topology with an orchestrator, round-robin, prompt-based or custom speaker selection, and gives all agents the full conversation history. C# has MaximumIterationCount, Python has termination_condition and max_rounds.

Agent Framework handoff is a mesh topology without a central orchestrator, the receiving agent takes full ownership, it is interactive by default, and autonomous mode takes a turn limit (WithAutonomousMode(turnLimit: 10) in C#).

In the OpenAI Agents SDK a handoff is exposed as a tool named transfer_to_<agent_name> by default, with options tool_name_override, tool_description_override, on_handoff, input_type, input_filter, is_enabled and nest_handoff_history.
OpenAI Swarm is labelled experimental and educational and is replaced by the OpenAI Agents SDK.

Magentic orchestration in Agent Framework has a manager that builds a task ledger, tracks progress and re-plans; the documentation sample sets max_round_count=10, max_stall_count=3 and max_reset_count=2, and offers a plan sign-off option.

Microsoft states it is untested how well Magentic orchestration performs outside the original Magentic-One design, the C# types are experimental (diagnostic MAAIW001), and the Azure guide (r9) says to avoid it for time-sensitive or deterministic tasks.

Magentic-One (submitted 2024-11-07) uses an Orchestrator that plans, tracks progress and re-plans, with agents for browser, files and code, and reports statistically competitive results on GAIA, AssistantBench and WebArena.

MAST has 14 failure modes in 3 categories (system design issues, inter-agent misalignment, task verification), MAST-Data holds 1,600+ annotated traces from 7 frameworks, and the taxonomy was built from 150 traces with kappa 0.88. First submitted 2025-03-17, revised 2025-10-26.

Manus reports the KV-cache hit rate as the most important production metric, an average input to output ratio near 100:1, and quotes cached input at $0.30 per MTok versus $3 uncached for a Claude model in 2025. A timestamp at the start of the system prompt kills cache hits.

On NoLiMa, 11 of 13 models claiming 128K or more fall below 50 percent of their short-context baseline at 32K, and GPT-4o drops from 99.3 to 69.7 percent. On RULER, only about half of 17 models keep satisfactory performance at 32K.
Claude context editing is in beta with header context-management-2025-06-27 and strategies clear_tool_uses_20250919 and clear_thinking_20251015, and server-side compaction is in beta.

Agent Framework's compaction is experimental, applies only to agents that keep history in memory (not Foundry agents or Responses API with store enabled), and treats a tool call and its results as one atomic message group.

Foundry Agent Service memory (preview, 2026-10-13) has user profile, chat summary and procedural types, limits of 100 scopes per store and 10,000 memories per scope, 1,000 search and 1,000 update requests per minute, no VNet support, item-level CRUD, a default TTL and remember-or-forget commands.

AgentPoison reports above 80 percent average attack success at a poison rate below 0.1 percent with under 1 percent impact on benign use, and MINJA plants malicious memories through ordinary queries with no direct write access.
GDPR Article 17 gives a right to erasure without undue delay where listed grounds apply, with exceptions in paragraph 3 such as legal obligations and legal claims.

Agent Framework workflow checkpoints are written at the end of each superstep and capture executor state, pending messages, pending requests and responses and shared state; Python 1.13.0 added entry checkpoints.

The Durable Extension for Agent Framework makes human-in-the-loop waits cost no compute or tokens (a 24-hour approval costs seconds of execution on Flex Consumption); install uses a prerelease flag (--prerelease for .NET, --pre for pip) and GA status is not stated on the page.
LangGraph interrupt() needs a checkpointer and a thread_id and waits until resumed with Command; InMemorySaver loses state on restart.
Stripe idempotency keys are client-generated up to 255 characters, retries with the same key return the saved response, and v1 keys can be pruned after at least 24 hours.
Agent Framework tool approval wraps a function in ApprovalRequiredAIFunction, and the run completes with a response that says what user input is required.
OWASP LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency names excessive functionality, excessive permissions and excessive autonomy as root causes.
